src: NOAA NHC/AOML HURDAT, NWS/SPC/NCEI, JMA, JTWC, IMD, BoM, Fiji Met Service, Météo-France, HKO, PAGASA, WMO, Met Office, KNMI, USGS, NPS, USACE, ReliefWeb, Copernicus
st: Burchardi flood tears the island of Strand apart
A North Sea storm surge on 11–12 Oct 1634 split Strand into Nordstrand and Pellworm; at least 6,123 drowned on Strand.
Great Storm of 1703 windstorm wrecks the Royal Navy
Destroyed the first Eddystone Lighthouse with its builder inside and sank many Royal Navy ships; Defoe wrote a book about it.
Great Natchez tornado sinks flatboats on the Mississippi
Second-deadliest US tornado: 269 of the dead were on the river after it tossed 116 of 120 docked flatboats into the water.
Indianola Hurricane wipes out a Texas port town
A 15 ft surge and fire leveled Indianola, Texas; its post office closed and the town was abandoned.
Yellow River flood, among deadliest in history
The Huang He broke its dikes in Henan in autumn 1887, flooding vast areas of the North China Plain.
WMO's record for hailstorm deaths; hailstones were described as large as goose eggs, oranges and cricket balls, and about 1,600 animals died.
Great Blizzard of 1888, the 'Great White Hurricane'
Up to 58 inches of snow and drifts over 50 feet paralyzed the US East Coast from the Chesapeake to Maine.
Johnstown flood after South Fork Dam failure
The South Fork Dam failed about 3:10 pm on 31 May 1889; the flood reached Johnstown at 4:07 pm. NPS says the true toll was probably over 3,000.
Great St. Louis–East St. Louis tornado
Third-deadliest US tornado on record; NOAA says it would likely rate EF4 today, with roughly $25 million in damage in 1896 dollars.
Cyclone Mahina wrecks the pearling fleet at Bathurst Bay
A surge of up to 13 m was reported in Princess Charlotte Bay; a 2014 study proposes a pressure near 880 hPa.
San Ciriaco Hurricane devastates Puerto Rico
Lasted about 28 days, the longest-lived Atlantic hurricane on record, and remains Puerto Rico's deadliest storm.
Typhoon strikes Hong Kong with under an hour's warning
Less than 30 minutes' warning was given; the disaster led the colony to develop an early warning system for the Observatory.
Great flood of Paris: Seine at 8.62 m
The Seine peaked at 8.62 m on the Austerlitz gauge on 28 Jan 1910 after about 10 days of rising water.
Death Valley heatwave sets 56.7 °C world record
Furnace Creek hit 56.7 °C (134 °F) on 10 July 1913, still the highest air temperature recognised by WMO.
Galveston Hurricane of 1915 tests the new seawall
First major test of the seawall built after 1900; the wall held, but waves hurled heavy granite blocks into city streets.
Swatow Typhoon drowns tens of thousands in south China
A surge of at least 12 ft swept Shantou; about 5,000 of its 65,000 residents died, and some 50,000 more died in the surrounding area.
Great Miami Hurricane strikes boomtown Miami
Normalized to 2018 conditions, its damage is estimated at about $236 billion, the costliest US hurricane on that basis.
Floodwater covered over 27,000 square miles in 10 states and left about 700,000 people homeless.
Cuba Hurricane of 1932 destroys Santa Cruz del Sur
A 6.5 m (21 ft) storm surge killed about 2,870 in Santa Cruz del Sur, the deadliest disaster in Cuban history.
Muroto Typhoon drives record storm surge into Osaka
Cape Muroto read 911.9 hPa, then a world low for a land station; a surge of 3-4 m flooded 49 km2 of Osaka.
1936 North American heatwave in the Dust Bowl
Many Illinois stations passed 110 °F; Bloomington reached an all-time record 114 °F (45.6 °C) on 15 July 1936.
Waco F5 tornado, deadliest in Texas since 1900
A 23-mile path through downtown Waco; 30 people died when a six-story furniture store collapsed, and over 600 buildings were destroyed.
Worcester F4 tornado strikes New England
On the ground for 78 minutes along 48 miles; debris was carried as far as Cape Cod, about 110 miles away.
North Sea flood: storm surge breaches dikes
A surge nearly 3 m high in Norfolk, and higher in the Netherlands, flooded about 200,000 ha of the Netherlands and 160,000 ha of England.
Hurricane Hazel hits the Carolinas and floods Toronto
Raced inland to Canada, where flooding killed 81 people, most of them in the Toronto area.
A 14.4 ft (4.4 m) surge in Narragansett Bay left downtown Providence under about 12 ft of water.
Chetumal's anemometer read 175 mph before it blew away; only four buildings in the town were left standing.
Hurricane Audrey floods Cameron Parish, Louisiana
Storm surge near 12 ft pushed up to 20 miles inland; most deaths occurred in Cameron Parish.
Typhoon Ida's Kanogawa floods kill over 1,200 in Japan
Tokyo received almost 430 mm of rain in one day, its highest daily total since records began in 1876.
The destruction of Belize City led the government to build a new inland capital, Belmopan, completed in 1970.
Hurricane Flora deluges Haiti and Cuba
Santiago de Cuba recorded 100.39 in (2,550 mm) of rain, the highest total ever measured in Cuba.
Palm Sunday outbreak: 17 violent F4 tornadoes
47 tornadoes hit the Midwest on 11 April 1965, including a famous twin-funnel tornado photographed near Dunlap, Indiana.
Florence flood: the Arno swamps Renaissance art
Floodwater reached 4.92 m in the Santa Croce district on 4 Nov 1966, damaging thousands of artworks and books.
Hurricane Camille (Category 5) slams the Mississippi coast
Storm surge reached about 24.6 ft (7.5 m) at Pass Christian; up to 27 in of rain later fell in Nelson County, Virginia.
Hurricane Agnes triggers record Susquehanna floods
Its rains brought record Susquehanna River flooding; at about $2.1 billion it was then the costliest US hurricane.
Iran blizzard, deadliest blizzard on record
A week of snow in February 1972 left up to 8 m of snow in rural Iran; villages such as Kakkan and Kumar were buried, with no survivors.
Cyclone Tracy flattens Darwin on Christmas Day
Darwin Airport logged a 217 km/h gust before its anemometer was destroyed; 45 died in the city and 21 at sea.
1974 Super Outbreak: 148 tornadoes, Xenia F5 tornado
148 tornadoes in 13 US states plus Ontario, with 30 rated F4–F5; an F5 tornado destroyed much of Xenia, Ohio.
A stalled storm dropped up to 7.5 inches of rain in about an hour, sending a flash flood through a crowded Colorado canyon.
Great Blizzard of 1978 sets Ohio pressure record
Cleveland's pressure fell to 28.28 inHg, Ohio's lowest ever; gusts reached 82 mph at Cleveland and 111 mph on Lake Erie.
Typhoon Tip sets the lowest sea-level pressure on record
Tip's pressure fell to 870 hPa and its gale-force winds spanned 2,220 km, the largest tropical cyclone ever observed.
Hurricane David (Category 5) strikes the Dominican Republic
Its eye passed almost directly over Santo Domingo; about 2,000 people died in the Dominican Republic.
Hurricane Allen, 190 mph Atlantic giant, reaches Texas
One of only two Atlantic hurricanes with 190 mph (305 km/h) sustained winds; it reached Category 5 three separate times.
Ivanovo F4 tornado, deadliest in Soviet history
Path of about 160 km; it threw a 50-tonne water tank 200 m. ESSL lowered the rating from F5 to F4 in 2018.
WMO-recognised heaviest hailstone, 1.02 kg (2.25 lb), fell in Gopalganj district, Bangladesh, on 14 April 1986.
Great Storm of 1987 windstorm fells 15 million trees
Gusts reached 100 knots at Shoreham, Sussex, and 119 knots in Brittany; about 15 million trees fell in southern England.
Hurricane Gilbert (Category 5) strikes the Yucatán Peninsula
Its 888 hPa was the lowest Atlantic pressure on record until Wilma (2005); the most intense cyclone known to strike Mexico.
Hurricane Hugo (Category 4) slams Charleston, South Carolina
Drove a 20.2 ft (6.2 m) storm surge at Seewee Bay, the highest storm tide recorded on the US East Coast.
Tropical Cyclone Thelma's flash flood buries Ormoc City
About 500 mm of rain fell in roughly three hours near Ormoc; 4,922 people died in the city alone.
Costliest US hurricane until Katrina at about $27 billion; a 2004 NOAA reanalysis upgraded it to Category 5.
Strongest hurricane on record to strike Hawaii; it destroyed 1,421 houses on Kauai and caused about $3.1 billion in damage.
Great flood of 1993 on the Mississippi
The Mississippi crested at a record 49.58 ft at St. Louis on 1 Aug 1993 and stayed above flood stage for 144 days.
56 inches of snow fell on Mount Le Conte, Tennessee, and gusts hit 144 mph on Mt Washington across 13 affected states.
Hurricane John, longest-lived Pacific hurricane, roams 31 days
Lasted 31 days and traveled about 13,180 km, crossing the International Date Line twice.
Hurricane Opal hits the Florida Panhandle
Peaked at 916 hPa, a pressure typical of a Category 5, while its winds stayed in the Category 4 range.
Midway Airport hit 106 °F (41 °C), the Chicago area's all-time high, with a heat index of 125 °F (52 °C) on 13 July.
Cyclone Olivia sets the world wind gust record
Barrow Island recorded a 408 km/h gust, confirmed by WMO in 2010 as the highest wind gust measured outside a tornado.
Hurricane Pauline unleashes deadly floods in Acapulco
Dumped about 16.9 in (430 mm) of rain on Acapulco in 24 hours, setting off deadly flash floods and mudslides.
Hurricane Linda peaks near Socorro Island at 185 mph
The most intense Eastern Pacific hurricane on record until Patricia (2015); models briefly forecast a turn toward California.
Great ice storm of 1998 in Quebec and Ontario
Up to 100 mm of freezing rain and ice pellets fell on 4–10 Jan 1998, cutting power to about 1.4 million Quebec customers.
Bridge Creek–Moore F5 tornado: record 486 km/h wind
Doppler on Wheels radar measured 135 m/s (302 mph), the WMO world record for tornado wind speed; path 38 miles long, up to 1 mile wide.
Lothar windstorm hits Paris with 169 km/h gusts
Gusts hit 169 km/h at Paris-Montsouris on 26 Dec 1999; in France alone about 176 million m3 of timber was felled.
Cyclone Eline compounds Mozambique's great flood
Eline lasted 29 days and travelled over 11,000 km, about a quarter of Earth's circumference.
Reports said no home was left standing on Tikopia, yet no deaths were reported; Zoe was 2002's most intense cyclone.
Cyclone Gafilo hits Madagascar at near-record strength
Gafilo deepened to 895 hPa; the ferry Samson capsized off Mahajanga and only 3 of its 120 listed aboard reached shore.
Hurricane Ivan makes landfall at Gulf Shores, Alabama
Spawned at least 118 tornadoes, the largest tropical-cyclone tornado outbreak on record; ravaged about 90% of Grenada's homes.
Hurricane Charley (Category 4) hits Punta Gorda, Florida
Strengthened from 110 to 145 mph in about three hours just before landfall; damage totaled about $16.9 billion.
Reached 2.5 miles wide along a 52-mile path and destroyed most of the village of Hallam, Nebraska.
Hurricane Wilma hits Florida after record 882 hPa peak
Lowest Atlantic pressure on record (882 hPa); Isla Mujeres measured 64.33 in (1,634 mm) of rain in 24 hours.
Hurricane Rita strikes the Texas-Louisiana border
Triggered an evacuation of 2.5 to 3.7 million people, the largest in US history.
Typhoon Saomai, strongest landfall on mainland China
China's weather agency rated it the strongest typhoon to strike the mainland; a Fuding station recorded a 273 km/h gust.
Cyclone Larry wipes out Australia's banana crop
Larry destroyed 80-90% of Australia's banana crop near Innisfail, and banana prices rose by 400-500%.
Wake Island was evacuated before Ioke damaged about 70% of its buildings; it had the lowest Central Pacific pressure on record.
Cyclone Sidr's surge sweeps southern Bangladesh
A surge over 5 m hit Patuakhali, Barguna and Jhalokati; aid agencies estimated up to 15,000 deaths.
Cyclone Gonu, strongest on record in the Arabian Sea
Gonu was the first super cyclonic storm recorded in the Arabian Sea and Oman's worst natural disaster on record.
Hurricane Dean (Category 5) strikes Mexico's Costa Maya
The first Category 5 landfall in the Atlantic basin since Andrew in 1992, with a dropsonde pressure of 905 hPa.
Struck Nicaragua's Mosquito Coast at Category 5, the southernmost Category 5 landfall on record in the Atlantic.
Greensburg EF5 tornado, the first EF5 ever rated
1.7 miles wide on a 28.8-mile track, with about 205 mph winds; destroyed about 95% of Greensburg, Kansas.
Gusts reached 202 km/h on the Wendelstein summit and 198 km/h on the Brocken as Kyrill crossed Europe on 18 January 2007.
87 tornadoes in nine states on 5–6 Feb 2008; an EF4 starting near Atkins, Arkansas left a 122-mile continuous damage path.
2008 southern China snowstorm and ice storm
Snow and ice at Lunar New Year stranded nearly 6 million rail passengers and toppled power towers across Hunan, Guizhou and nearby provinces.
Typhoon Morakot dumps nearly 3 m of rain on Taiwan
Rainfall peaked at 2,777 mm; a mudslide buried Xiaolin village, killing about 400 of its residents.
PAGASA's Science Garden gauge logged 454.9 mm in 24 hours, flooding much of Metro Manila.
Melbourne topped 43 °C three days running in late January, then reached a record 46.4 °C on Black Saturday, 7 Feb 2009.
Red Dawn dust storm turns Sydney orange
On 23 Sept 2009, PM10 hit 15,366 µg/m3 at Bringelly, Sydney's highest ever; about 2.5 Mt of dust was lost off the coast.
Vivian hailstorm: record 20 cm US hailstone
The record US hailstone measured 8.0 in (20 cm) across and weighed 0.88 kg (1.94 lb), Western Hemisphere's heaviest.
2010 Pakistan floods cover a fifth of the country
At their peak, monsoon floods covered about one-fifth of Pakistan's land area and affected about 18 million people.
Moscow hit 38.2 °C on 29 July 2010; July was its hottest month in over 130 years, and peat fires choked the city.
Cyclone Yasi crosses Queensland at Mission Beach
Pressure fell to 929 hPa as the eye passed Tully; damage of about A$3.5 billion made it Australia's costliest cyclone.
2011 Super Outbreak: 362 tornadoes incl. Hackleburg EF5
362 confirmed tornadoes in four days, three of them EF5; WMO lists 27 April's 209 tornadoes as the largest one-day outbreak.
1.5 miles wide with winds of about 190 mph; it tracked 80.3 miles through Tuscaloosa and Birmingham, injuring over 1,000.
Joplin EF5 tornado, deadliest US tornado since 1947
Winds over 200 mph along a 21.6-mile track up to 1 mile wide; at $2.8 billion, the costliest single tornado in US history.
Seven major industrial estates were flooded; the World Bank put losses at 1.425 trillion baht (about US$46 billion).
A dust wall at least 5,000–6,000 ft tall and nearly 100 miles wide swept across metro Phoenix on 5 July 2011, cutting visibility to near zero.
Bopha reached Category 5 at 7.4°N, the second-most southerly on record, and was the strongest storm ever to hit Mindanao.
Cyclone Phailin strikes Odisha after mass evacuation
More than 550,000 people were evacuated from the Odisha and Andhra Pradesh coasts before landfall near Gopalpur.
El Reno tornado: widest on record at 4.2 km (EF3)
2.6 miles (4,184 m) wide, a WMO record; mobile RaXPol radar measured winds of at least 295 mph near the ground.
Extreme June rain and a flood from Chorabari Lake swept through the Kedarnath pilgrimage town on 16–17 June 2013.
Super Typhoon Rammasun hits Hainan at full strength
A station on Qizhou Island near landfall read 899.2 hPa, the lowest sea-level pressure ever recorded in China.
Pam passed just east of Efate at 896 hPa intensity; Erromango and Tanna suffered catastrophic damage.
Hurricane Patricia, strongest winds on record, hits Jalisco
Its 215 mph (345 km/h) winds are the highest reliably estimated in any tropical cyclone; 872 hPa is a Western Hemisphere record.
2015 India heatwave in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
Titlagarh reached 47.6 °C as late-May heat killed thousands, mostly in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
Super Typhoon Meranti batters tiny Itbayat island
Meranti's 890 hPa was the lowest Western Pacific pressure since 2010; it later struck Xiamen, killing about 45 in east China.
Cyclone Winston strikes Fiji at Category 5
Winston struck Viti Levu as the most intense Southern Hemisphere cyclone on record; Vanua Balavu logged a 306 km/h gust.
Reached Category 5 at 13.4°N, the lowest latitude on record for an Atlantic storm of that strength.
Hurricane Irma strikes the Florida Keys
Held Category 5 strength for 60 consecutive hours, second in the Atlantic only to the 1932 Cuba hurricane.
Super Typhoon Mangkhut slams Luzon and Hong Kong
Hong Kong held Signal No. 10 for ten hours as a surge of up to 3.38 m and 220 km/h gusts struck Waglan Island.
Typhoon Jebi floods Kansai Airport and cuts its bridge
A tanker struck the airport's only bridge; Osaka's 3.29 m surge broke the 1961 record and Kansai logged a 209 km/h gust.
Dropped 35.93 in (913 mm) of rain near Elizabethtown, the wettest tropical cyclone on record in North Carolina.
Hurricane Michael (Category 5) strikes Mexico Beach, Florida
First Category 5 landfall in the contiguous US since Andrew; inundation reached 14 ft above ground at Mexico Beach.
Hurricane Lane drenches Hawaii's Big Island
Wettest tropical cyclone on record in Hawaii; Hilo had its wettest three days on record with 31.85 in (809 mm).
Typhoon Hagibis becomes Japan's costliest typhoon
JMA recorded a 55 hPa pressure fall in 12 hours; damage above US$17 billion made it Japan's costliest typhoon in nominal terms.
Typhoon Lekima triggers deadly landslides in Zhejiang
A landslide in Yongjia County blocked a river, raising water 10 m in ten minutes; Wenling recorded a 221 km/h gust.
Cyclone Fani hits Puri as 1.2 million evacuate
Odisha moved over 1.2 million people to shelters before the strongest storm to hit the state since 1999.
Cyclone Kenneth, strongest landfall in Mozambique's history
Kenneth struck six weeks after Idai, only the second time two intense cyclones hit Mozambique in one season.
Hurricane Dorian (Category 5) stalls over the Bahamas
Stalled over Grand Bahama for about a day with surge up to 23 ft; the strongest hurricane on record to strike the Bahamas.
Super Typhoon Goni makes the strongest landfall on record
Goni struck Bato, Catanduanes, with 1-minute winds of 315 km/h, the highest landfall intensity ever recorded.
Super Cyclone Amphan strikes the Ganges Delta
Amphan was the strongest cyclone recorded in the Ganges Delta; damage of about US$15.5 billion was a North Indian record at the time.
Typhoon Rai (Odette) slams Siargao in December
Rai was the strongest December landfall recorded in the Philippines and the country's second-costliest cyclone after Haiyan.
Hurricane Ida strikes Port Fourchon, Louisiana
Its remnants prompted the first flash flood emergencies ever issued for northeastern New Jersey and New York City.
Western Kentucky EF4 with winds of about 190 mph, on the ground for 165.7 miles and up to 1.13 miles wide in a rare December outbreak.
Ahr valley flood in western Europe
Rain on 14 July 2021 was the highest in the ERA5 record (since 1950) for the Belgian–German border region; the Ahr valley was devastated.
Zhengzhou flood: 201.9 mm of rain in one hour
Zhengzhou got 201.9 mm in one hour on 20 July 2021, a Chinese record; 14 people died in a flooded metro train.
Monsoon rain was nearly 2.9 times the 30-year national average; over 33 million people were affected and about 8 million displaced.
UK heatwave breaks 40 °C for the first time
Coningsby reached 40.3 °C on 19 July 2022; 46 UK stations met or beat the previous national record of 38.7 °C.
Typhoon Doksuri brings Beijing its heaviest rain on record
Its remnants dropped 744.8 mm at Wangjiayuan Reservoir, Beijing's highest total since records began in 1883.
Cyclone Mocha slams Sittwe on the Myanmar coast
The JTWC estimated 1-minute winds of 270 km/h, a Category 5-equivalent storm, before landfall just north of Sittwe.
Cyclone Freddy, the longest-lived tropical cyclone ever
Freddy lasted 36 days and travelled 12,785 km from Australia to Africa, a duration record certified by WMO.
Cyclone Gabrielle triggers New Zealand's national emergency
New Zealand declared only its third national state of emergency; damage of US$9.2 billion is a Southern Hemisphere record.
Strengthened by 105 mph in 21 hours and became the first Eastern Pacific hurricane on record to make landfall at Category 5.
Rolling Fork EF4 tornado levels Mississippi town
An EF4 with winds of about 170 mph on a 59.4-mile path up to 3/4 mile wide through the Mississippi Delta at night.
Derna flood after Storm Daniel bursts two dams
Both dams above Derna failed after midnight on 11 Sept 2023, releasing over 30 million m3 of water into the city.
Super Typhoon Yagi hits Vietnam, its worst in 70 years
Yagi reached Category 5 twice, the strongest storm recorded in the South China Sea, and became Vietnam's costliest cyclone.
Pamandzi Airport on Mayotte recorded a 226 km/h gust; Météo-France called it the strongest storm there in at least 90 years.
Hurricane Milton makes landfall at Siesta Key, Florida
Pressure fell 82 hPa in about 17 hours to 895 hPa, tying Rita for the lowest pressure recorded in the Gulf of Mexico.
Hurricane Beryl, earliest Category 5, hits Carriacou
Became the earliest Category 5 hurricane on record in the Atlantic, breaking Emily's July 16, 2005 mark.
Chiva received 491 mm of rain in eight hours on 29 Oct 2024, roughly a year's worth, according to AEMET.
Tied Allen for the strongest Atlantic sustained winds (190 mph) and became the strongest hurricane on record to strike Jamaica.
